statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of seven representative public paths. Authenticated account, broker order execution, payment completion and every localized/template variant were outside scope.

page.framework: Large server-rendered multi-page site plus JavaScript/canvas SPA chart application

paths.description: Public landing page and global navigation; represents marketing, market-summary and consent surfaces.
Supercharts primary application journey; represents the core interactive research task and long-lived SPA behavior.
Markets index; represents a dense listing and navigation archetype.
Apple symbol detail; represents instrument detail, data formatting and structured metadata.
Community ideas listing; represents public editorial/community content and crawler rendering.
Pricing and subscription entry; represents commercial commitments and plan comparison.
Deliberate unknown route; represents HTTP/navigation recovery.

findings.summary: System dark preference does not select a dark theme
findings.evidence: The CSS capability probe found 0 prefers-color-scheme rules, and the DOM reported color-scheme: light. The dark-emulated capture was pixel-identical to the default capture rather than being selected from the operating-system preference.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map page surfaces and controls through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while retaining any explicit user override.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion users still receive continuous animation
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() reported a running 3.5 s hero animation and twenty 1 s skeleton animations; the CSS probe found 0 prefers-reduced-motion rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduce media query that removes nonessential hero/ambient motion and replaces repeating skeleton motion with a static state or minimal opacity change.

findings.summary: Consent banner consumes a large part of the mobile first viewport
findings.evidence: The 360x800 screenshot shows the cookie banner occupying roughly the bottom 84 px and overlaying the hero on every fresh visit. It is dismissible and offers balanced choices, but still interrupts the first view.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve non-overlapping space for the consent surface or use a less obstructive compact presentation while keeping equally prominent accept and decline actions.

findings.summary: Some touch targets are too small or tightly spaced
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found multiple 16–20 px-high broker and footer targets below the 24 px minimum and reported the target-size audit as failing.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the clickable box and spacing of small links/buttons to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary mobile controls, without shrinking visible labels.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly prevents user zoom
findings.evidence: The live meta viewport is width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0, minimum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no; Lighthouse failed the meta-viewport accessibility audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and the maximum/minimum scale restrictions, then verify reflow and controls at 200% and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: Cold mobile load is slow and main-thread heavy
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.9 s, FCP 7.4 s, TBT 530 ms and time-to-interactive 20.7 s (performance 0.45). The raw-CDP trace was faster locally but still found long tasks; the chart trace had LCP 3.76 s and 232 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP resource, delay noncritical application and advertising work, and split/chunk long tasks until lab LCP and interaction latency reach the good range.

findings.summary: Critical delivery fans out into hundreds of CSS and JavaScript requests
findings.evidence: The homepage HAR recorded 464 requests including 194 stylesheets and 131 scripts; the chart recorded 977 requests, 458 stylesheets and 465 scripts, with 6.29 MB transferred. Parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets form a long blocking candidate list.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate the critical CSS path, preload only proven critical assets, defer conditional chart modules, and cap initial route request fan-out.

findings.summary: Large unused and third-party JavaScript ships on initial load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 524 KiB of unused JavaScript, including 153 KiB from the ad script, 87 KiB from toast-layer, 73 KiB from Google identity and 136 KiB across two tag-manager bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Load advertising, identity and toast code only when the relevant surface is requested; deduplicate analytics bootstraps and route-split application bundles.

findings.summary: Images, canvas content and controls are not consistently exposed to assistive technology
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt; the images probe found 91/100 sampled homepage images and 87/100 symbol-page images without alt. The chart has 20 canvases with no fallback text and 35 of 193 buttons without text, aria-label or title.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images concise alt text, mark decoration alt="", name every control, and expose chart values/summary/table equivalents outside canvas.

findings.summary: The chart application has no heading structure and focus indication is inconsistent
findings.evidence: The rendered chart contained no h1–h6 elements. A focus probe across the landing page found most sampled controls with outline-style none, while only one sampled control displayed a 2 px focus outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise page heading/landmark model to the chart shell and ensure every interactive control receives a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator in logical keyboard order.

findings.summary: Initial load logs errors and uses a deprecated unload listener
findings.evidence: Lighthouse logged a Google Identity FedCM NetworkError and a not-signed-in error. It also found an unload event listener, which is deprecated and contributes to two BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat expected signed-out identity state without console.error, remove unload listeners in favor of pagehide/visibility lifecycle patterns, and resolve BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Rendered images omit intrinsic dimensions
findings.evidence: The image primitive found width and height attributes absent on all 100 sampled images on both the homepage and symbol page. Observed CLS was low in this run, but the markup does not reserve intrinsic image space.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or an equivalent aspect-ratio for every image at render time and retain responsive CSS sizing.

findings.summary: The public chart route is nearly empty to non-JavaScript crawlers
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 1% raw-to-rendered content coverage for /chart/, classified it as a JS shell, and found that the rendered dynamic title was absent from raw HTML. Homepage, ideas and symbol pages were substantially server-rendered.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render a stable chart title, heading, symbol summary and key values, then hydrate the interactive chart progressively.

findings.summary: A generic link label and zoom restriction weaken mobile/crawlable navigation
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO was 0.85 and flagged the link text “More”; its mobile accessibility audit also failed because viewport zoom is disabled. Robots and sitemap otherwise expose public routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace “More” with destination-specific text and remove viewport zoom restrictions.

findings.summary: Browser security policy and cookie flags can be tightened
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and frame-ancestors none are present, but CSP includes unsafe-inline in default-src; Permissions-Policy is absent; two non-auth cookies lacked Secure and all four observed cookies used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-inline where nonce/hash coverage permits, send a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and mark HTTPS cookies Secure with Lax/Strict SameSite unless cross-site behavior is required.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising code loads before a consent choice
findings.evidence: On a fresh profile while the consent banner was visible, trackers identified Tag Manager, DoubleClick and Google Ads. The HAR attributed 3.11 MB of 3.34 MB to non-main origins, including about 564 KB for tag-manager/ad scripts, before the user accepted.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential analytics and advertising requests behind explicit consent, minimize vendors/events, and batch necessary telemetry.

findings.summary: The core chart route has no useful no-JavaScript baseline
findings.evidence: The rendered chart exposes thousands of characters of symbol and market data, but raw HTML contains only 67 text characters and 1% of rendered content words. The crawler screenshot is effectively an empty shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship a server-rendered symbol snapshot and core navigation as the baseline, then enhance it with real-time canvas interaction when JavaScript is available.

findings.summary: Some imagery is oversized and below-fold assets load eagerly
findings.evidence: The homepage image probe found two hero assets over 2x display width, 55 below-fold images without lazy loading, 22 without responsive sources and 20 legacy-format assets. The symbol page found 11 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide correctly sized AVIF/WebP srcsets, lazy-load below-fold imagery, and avoid downloading desktop-scale hero assets for narrow viewports.

findings.summary: Initial routes perform disproportionate background and conditional work
findings.evidence: The chart HAR made 977 requests and transferred 6.29 MB, overwhelmingly application scripts; the homepage fetched a 192 KB month-long economic calendar payload and multiple analytics endpoints during initial rendering.
findings.suggestedFix: Fetch chart modules and secondary datasets on demand, narrow initial calendar queries, and move nonessential background fetches behind idle/visibility/user-intent gates.

findings.summary: Heavy media and third parties dominate the landing-page budget
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a 6,859 KiB page payload led by a 3.65 MB WebM video, while advertising, analytics and identity scripts added hundreds of KiB before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a poster/static first frame by default, defer the WebM until visible and motion-allowed, and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.
